question: What hexadecimal or Pantone color code does the MUTCD prescribe for the red background of a STOP sign?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not contain any hexadecimal or Pantone color code for the red background of a STOP sign, and the MUTCD text supplied does not prescribe such codes. The MUTCD's Color Code section assigns only the general *meaning* of colors (red means "stop or prohibition"); precise color specifications are not present in the evidence, which instead refers detailed sign design matters to the "Standard Highway Signs" publication. Standards (mandatory): - "The general meaning of the 13 colors shall be as follows: … K. Red—stop or prohibition …" — this establishes what red signifies, not a numeric color specification. - "The sign dimensions prescribed in the sign size tables in the various Parts and Chapters in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used unless engineering judgment determines that other sizes are appropriate…" — the MUTCD defers detailed design specifications to the companion "Standard Highway Signs" publication, but the evidence contains no color-code values. Citations: - Section 1D.05 Standard §2 (p.33) - Section 2A.07 Standard §2 (p.45) - Table 2A-2 (p.43) - Page 89 - Page 94 Note: Based on the evidence available, I cannot identify a hexadecimal or Pantone code — the MUTCD evidence here defines color meanings and usage, not colorimetric specifications.
